title: Onramp curriculum and telemetry pipeline for SDK sample apps
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a repeatable onramp curriculum composed of SDK sample apps, guided quickstarts, and a telemetry pipeline that captures activation and retention signals. This initiative ties to OKR: Increase new developer activation and 14-day retention for SDK users by 35% in Q2. Deliverables: curated sample app gallery (multi-language), step-by-step guided onramp flows, instrumentation spec, and dashboarding for activation funnels and cohort retention. Coordinate with Engineering (SDK owners), Design (sample UX), and DX Content writers.
acceptance_criteria: A public sample app gallery with at least 6 canonical patterns implemented across JS, Python, and Go
Guided quickstart flow embedded in Console docs with one-click deploy or reproducible local dev path
Telemetry schema defined and implemented for the three core events: onboarding_started, sample_run_success, and sdk_key_first_call
A working dashboard in the Console or Looker showing activation funnel and 14-day retention cohorts
Playbook describing experiment matrix and tactics to increase retention (caching tips, snippet variants, onboarding emails)
success_metrics: New developer activation rate (signup -> sdk_key_first_call) increases 35% vs baseline
14-day retention (users who call SDK again within 14 days) improves by 25%
Time-to-first-successful-sample reduced to under 20 minutes for new signups
At least two retention experiments launched and instrumented during cycle
tasks: Draft content outline and map to sample apps (PM + Docs)
Design UX mocks for sample gallery and guided flow (Design)
Implement canonical sample apps and release NPM/PyPI packages (Engineering SDK)
Add telemetry events to SDK templates and quickstarts (Engineering + Observability)
Create dashboards and alerts for activation funnel (Data/Analytics)
Define experiment backlog and instrumentation gating (PM)
Write rollout plan: canary experiment cohorts, messaging, and success criteria
